text: Hi, I'm Aishwarya from the MicroStrategy team. This video walks through the fluency trap in a variance note and the phase gate that catches it before a fluent sounding claim gets treated as verified evidence. Revenue is down this

title: The Fluent-Wrong Note
text: Quarter because enterprise renewals slipped. That sentence has no source behind it and it was about to go in a board deck. Method, a variance note

title: Method: What a Variance Note Needs
text: Becomes evidence only when it ties to a source, a period, and an owner who can be asked how they know. Use this test before anything goes in a deck. Where it fails, a fluent sentence and a sourced sentence look identical on the page. The confidence of the language tells you nothing about whether the underlying number was ever checked. The fix is

title: The Fix: Preparation vs. Judgment
text: Structural, not a reminder to be careful. A phase gate splits preparation from judgment. The machine drafts, computes, and flags. A named human reads the flagged items, ties them to a source, and decides if the note is ready. The gate is not a formality. It is the point where accountability actually enters the artifact. Verified means four things exist together. A

title: What "Verified" Requires
text: Named source file, the period it covers, a control total that ties to the general ledger, and an owner who will stand behind the number. Missing any one of these, the sentence is an assertion, not evidence, no matter how confident it sounds. Your turn. Take

title: Your Turn: Audit a Real Variance Note
text: A variance note you've actually seen go into a deck and paste it in with this prompt. Pull out every factual claim and for each one, name the source, period, and owner it would need to count as verified or mark it unsupported. Read what comes back before you trust any of it.
